justification: A dies on absence: no price is ever quoted or tracked, and 'nine harvests' is the span of the fire log, not a price series - the only pricing phrase, 'so much per ton per point of moisture', is an aside about who buys mixed-flow machines. B is the strongest lure because Grendisham's unmanned-site objection is real and the writer endorses its force ('it cannot be answered from files like these'), but it dies on scope: the whole of para 1 (the reputation, the count, the fines explanation) and the whole of para 4 (Steadgrove's dates and the contract) lie outside it, so it names one rebuttal inside a four-way dispute. C dies on absence of any advocacy: the text reports that a mixed-flow 'goes to operations drying for their neighbors as well as themselves' as demography, never recommending that farms dry their own.

A is flatly reversed by 'per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent'. C borrows the words 'swabbed clean in September' from Grendisham's rebuttal, but those describe her crews' seasonal experience, not Calverend's sample; his sample is killed by 'The first thing he found was dirt', and 'newest' has no referent anywhere since machine age is never mentioned. D (small-n objection) is raised by nobody: Steadgrove 'accepts the swabs', the writer calls them 'hard to walk past', and 'nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground'.

A misreads 'Set those two numbers side by side' as agreement, but the same sentence continues 'and of course the fire looks late' - she asserts a gap, not a match. B dies on absence: her complaint concerns what the call-in time means, never which machines the fire department's log covers. D ('never intended to be read as evidence at all') is an absolute overreach - she assigns the time a definite evidential meaning, 'that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught', i.e. evidence of noticing rather than of ignition, which is exactly what C states.

B fails the arithmetic on the page: 'Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch' out of sixty-one leaves twelve fires outside it, which is not 'hardly a fire'. C is killed explicitly by 'Steadgrove's is not the mutual's to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators'. D leans on 'trucks waiting' in the closing scene, but that is one operator at one site, and the text names a contractual driver - 'the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing' - never an arrival rate exceeding drying capacity; the key is anchored instead in 'the machine stops mattering', i.e. pressure that is machine-independent.

A is contradicted by 'Grendisham's objection has not been answered'. B (neutral reporter) is the strongest lure given the closing rhetorical question, but the final paragraph is openly evaluative - 'The swabs are hard to walk past', 'his objection has not been answered', 'Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it' - so she does not withhold judgement. D is killed by 'Whether writing a run-on clause into next year's policies would be worth anything turns on something nobody has worked out how to check'.

All three are near-synonyms of 'view' that fail the fixed idiom 'take the long view': A 'take the long outlook' is not an English collocation despite 'long-term outlook' being one; B 'take the long gaze' names a literal stare where the context ('twelve years from a key') demands the figurative patience sense; D 'take the long sight' trades on the real adjective 'long-sighted' but the noun phrase does not exist.

A 'Increasingly' needs a trend in the rule, but the rule is fixed - 'That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it'. C 'Curiously' is pre-empted lexically by the same sentence: 'nobody disputes it or finds it odd'. D 'Privately' inverts the essay's public/private axis - the clause is the public letter of the rule ('Nothing here is hidden'), while the private dimension is the practice that works around it - and the key 'Strictly' is what licenses the following 'It is simply not what the list runs on'.

The slot is the fixed idiom 'waiting for dead men's shoes', whose meaning (advancement only through another's death) is exactly the paragraph's subject - movement comes when 'a winter that settles it'. B 'coats', C 'gloves' and D 'hats' are all garments a dead man might leave, but none forms an English idiom, and the sentence is explicitly quoting a set phrase ('The older hands have a phrase for this').

The frame 'not approving, but it is not ___ either' requires the opposite pole of approval, which only 'censorious' supplies. A 'gracious' sits on the same pole as approving, so the correlative 'but ... either' collapses into redundancy. B is the strongest lure (a committee giving an irregular succession 'one line' does look wary), but 'cautious' is not the antonym of 'approving', and a one-line minute of unapproving tone is if anything cautious, so denying it contradicts the sentence's own description. C 'anxious' fails the same structural test and has no anchor - no unease is attributed to the committee anywhere.

The collocation is 'invoke a rule'. A 'summoned' shares the calling-forth sense but never takes a rule as object. B 'provoked' is a phonetic near-miss and means elicit-by-irritation, not cite-as-authority. D 'evoked' is the intended discrimination and the strongest lure, but 'evoke' takes memories, feelings or images, never a rule appealed to as authority; the context - 'The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list' followed by three unpunished refusals - requires the cite-and-apply sense.

B imports real-world knowledge about rain and bird exclusion, but the text supplies its own because-clause for the narrowed mouth - 'since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening' - i.e. draught, and 'mainly' overreaches besides. C transposes the true claim onto the wrong variable: 'Pattern tells you very little', with three reasons given (yard stock, ornament, the 1961 rebuild), while 'Height is the part worth reading'. D is killed twice: 'Builders' yards sold whatever was in stock' and 'the pots seldom match', and the ornament was bought 'to tell their own door from thirty identical ones' - to differentiate, not to match.

findings: A: the passage foregrounds a purely time-based allowance ('threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves') and then shows the chandler's seven extra morning hours buying only 22 extra letters, so an allowance-farming reading is available and does not formally contradict the key.
justification: B and C die cleanly: B on the two numbers themselves (412 against 390 is 5.6 per cent, not 'far more'), and C on 'Both shut when the evening cart went at eight', which forbids anyone staying open after the cart. A is the problem. Argued at full strength: the keeper is paid solely for time and not at all for letters, which is a stated, undisguised incentive to hold the hatch open; the chandler opened at seven and was paid for thirteen hours; and the returns show that those seven pre-two hours yielded only 22 letters more than the bookseller's six-hour day, so the early opening looks economically pointless except as a way of earning the allowance. A test-taker who asks why the payment rule is in the passage at all will land here. It is nevertheless killable, on three grounds. First, the option says 'The keepers' - both of them - and the bookseller, paid on identical terms, opened at two; if the allowance drove behaviour he would have opened at seven too, so the plural is falsified by the very case that makes the item work. Second, 'stretched' presupposes a baseline the text never gives: no normal or contracted opening hour is stated, so nothing marks seven in the morning as a stretch rather than ordinary shop hours. Third, the surveyor - the officer who would police such abuse - 'remarked only that the chandler's flap wanted a new spring'. The key remains strictly better because it answers the comparative question the numbers are built to raise (13 hours against 6 producing near-identical counts, with a shared eight o'clock endpoint), whereas A explains only one house and only by imputing a motive the text never states. Flag rather than kill: A is survivable with effort and is not mutually exclusive with D, but it is not defensible as a second correct answer.

A fails on both season and order: 'Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten' (not vårvintern) and 'Först därefter rostades den', i.e. roasting came after the winter in the heap, not before it. B dies on the explicit negation 'Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt'. D is contradicted twice: 'Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte' is categorical, and the work was timed to dry ground, 'när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan', so wetter ground could not be the exemption.

B is the plain inversion of 'De blåsningar som drevs hårdast ... gav inte större luppar utan sprödare'. C overreaches on 'Samtliga' and 'misslyckades': the same span says the hard-driven blowings still produced luppar, only more brittle ones, and the paragraph reports 'Två resultat är tydliga' from all thirty-six runs. D is an attribution error and the strongest lure, since slow drying of the furnace is indeed in the text - but it sits in the descriptive paragraph on the excavated furnace type ('Innan den kunde fyllas måste den torkas långsamt'), not among Tolvsäter's two stated findings, which concern hard driving and the necessity of iron-rich slag.

A can borrow 'Ugnen kostade lera, sten och ved' and even the 1880s records of bogs being reworked, but the dating sentence closes it: 'Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet', so nothing supports 'långt in på 1800-talet'. B inverts the contrast - it is the later hyttan that 'krävde vattenkraft och ständig drift'. C trades on the word 'utförliga', but the same clause scopes it against the option: the uppteckningar are 'utförliga om vem som ägde vad' and 'säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen'.

A states Krokvall's reading ('ett tecken på dålig kontroll') and its first half is even true, but the text adjudicates against the causal clause: 'Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt; det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot', and 'Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet'. C is killed by the same sentence - 'Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt' - so the figures are not in dispute. D is a compound that fails on both limbs: iron content is a proportion and is never linked to heap volume (the varp is 'i ton' from centuries of blowings), and the between-site variation is placed in the explicitly unresolved paragraph, 'Mycket är ändå oklart ... varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen'; moreover the experiments make iron-rich slag a universal precondition, so it cannot discriminate between sites.

A can build on the demolished revenue forecast (31 per cent payment at the comparable site, weaker incentives at the bryggan), but the author rejects the mechanism outright - 'Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst' and 'Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten' - and a higher fee would worsen her distributional objection rather than fix it. B dies on the equipment list she demands (two new bojar with kastlina, a new stege, a hjärtstartare, plus a kastlina at Stångklippan) and on 'har alltså ingen annan utrustning än sina händer'. C is the direct opposite of 'Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst'.

B shifts the attribution: the difficulty of observing payment belongs to the bryggan ('varken bom, vakt eller registreringsskylt'), whereas the ställplats was in fact measured - 'Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna'. C inverts that same figure. D has no anchor at all: the arrangement is described as still in place since it was introduced 'för två somrar sedan', and no sign is ever said to have been removed.

A revives the kassör hypothesis that the investigation disposes of - 'Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså' - and is the direct opposite of the finding span. B is the strongest lure because the tjugotal överstrykningar are real, but the text refuses exactly that inference: 'överstrykningarna kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning - materialet svarar inte på det'. C is killed literally by 'Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord, ingen anvisning om längd'.

A is reversed by 'Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt'. C is the strongest lure, since the essay closes on residuals (the four hemmansägare, the two widows, and 'materialet svarar inte på det'), but those are conceded after the verdict is delivered - 'den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar' - and the concessive 'Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop' scopes the undecidability to details, not to the question of who chose the titles. D fails because her own explanation is not retained alongside the ordinary one but eliminated: 'Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså'.
